title: .NET reading: 1,000,000 rows, memory
dataset: 1,000,000 rows × 10 columns, written by the Hypaxel writer with inline or shared strings, read cell by cell
method: Allocations are for one run of the --read-quick stopwatch runner. Peak RSS comes from a separate process per reader (--read-quick 1000000 <reader> <inline|shared> under /usr/bin/time -l) and covers the whole process, including the runtime. Every reader produces the same checksum. The machine was otherwise idle.
notes: Allocations are the same on the other runtimes, except MiniExcel's (10.0 to 13.3 GB per read); peak RSS was measured on .NET 10 only.
With inline strings, the only allocations are the strings you ask for: the 153 MB are the 3M cell strings, and reading text as a span allocates nothing.
With shared strings, the 92 MB are the shared string table (1M distinct strings), which is loaded once and then read without allocating. Nothing else grows with the number of rows.
reproduce:
cd dotnet/benchmarks/Hypaxel.Benchmarks
dotnet run -c Release -f net10.0 -- --read-quick 1000000                    # all readers, both files
dotnet run -c Release -f net10.0 -- --read-quick 1000000 Sylvan shared      # one reader, one file
